stem.en: A group has no written laws and no court records. Yet two families settle a boundary dispute, and both accept the result and go on living side by side. Which explanation best fits a society of this kind?

text.en: The chief is the strongest man in the group, so nobody dares to disagree with him.
A record of the settlement must have been kept somewhere, because only writing can bind people.
Customs and practices accepted by the group give the settlement its force.
Each family has its own law, so no shared rule was needed.

explanation.en: A society is regulated mainly by customs and practices rather than by formal laws. So a settlement can hold when the group accepts the custom behind it, even if nothing is written down.

hints.en: What regulates a society when it has no formal laws?
Both families accepted the result, and nothing was written. What could make them accept it?
